VibePascal v55 -- x86_64-darwin native compiler (runs on Intel macOS).
-FU/-FE output directories are created instead of aborting the build.
Source commit: eae5d3e919 (merge of fix/output-dir-autocreate)
Compiler fix:  4d10b26fe772dfbd4992cbeb53f09028f7dfee4f
Parent release: v54 (b7d2d9676ecf1d7d8250cd460b9c48069920513e)
Built: 2026-09-10, cross-built on x86_64-linux against MacOSX26.2.sdk
Binary: bin/ppcx64  md5 29f2a740e3e79c1dd168843d0ad0f7e8

COMPILER BINARY ONLY.  Only compiler/options.pas changed between v54 and v55:
no RTL change, no package change, no PPU format change, so an existing v54
(or v53) x86_64-darwin unit set stays valid and the utility binaries are
unchanged and not re-shipped.

WHAT CHANGED
  -FE and -FU name where the COMPILER writes.  Up to and including v54 a
  missing one was an error: -FE reported 'Path "x/" does not exist' during
  option processing, and -FU failed later and far more obscurely at object
  write time ("Can't create assembler file: x/hello.s").  In both cases the
  compiler knew the path and made the user run mkdir.  v55 creates both
  directories up front, recursively.  An IMPOSSIBLE path (a component that is
  a plain file, a read-only parent) still stops the build with the same
  message -- now reported only after creation has been TRIED and FAILED, so it
  arrives early and names the directory.

  The fix shipped to Win64 first because that is where it was reported, then
  to Linux x86_64 and aarch64-linux.  Nothing about it is OS-specific.

HOW FAR THE VERIFICATION GOES ON THIS TARGET -- READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING IT
  This binary has NEVER BEEN EXECUTED.  The build host is x86_64-linux and
  there is no macOS on it, so nobody here can run a Mach-O.  That was equally
  true of the v54 binary this one replaces; it is not a new gap, but it is a
  real one and it is not going to be closed by anything on this machine.

  What IS established:
    - Format and architecture: runs on Intel macOS, Mach-O, checked with
      `file` on the exact bytes in this tarball.
    - The fix is compiled in, by Mach-O section triage against the published
      v54 binary (md5 c2e5bf6967f0d1fa8caf06155a645e46): __text grows 3575787 -> 3583563
      bytes, which is the added directory-creation code, while __DATA,__const
      is byte-identical.  The tarball is SMALLER than v54's only because the
      symbol table shrank (28675 -> 23866 symbols); no content was lost.
    - The BEHAVIOUR of this exact source was A/B proven elsewhere: natively on
      x86_64-linux against the published pre-fix v54 binary, and on
      aarch64-linux under qemu-user (baseline 4/11 corners, fixed 11/11, with
      every emitted binary executed rather than merely linked, and both
      must-refuse corners still refusing).

  What is NOT established: that this binary starts, compiles, or links on a
  Mac.  If you have a macOS box, the one number worth sending back is the exit
  code of `./bin/ppcx64 -iV` (expect 0, printing 3.3.1) -- it needs no SDK
  and no unit set to answer that.
